claims.statement: For a fixed finite-volume thermal network with C=C^T positive definite, K=K^T positive semidefinite, and matched port profiles b_i used both for heat-power injection and temperature measurement, H_ij(s)=b_i^T(K+sC)^(-1)b_j is symmetric under source/receiver exchange for every real s>0; its causal impulse response is symmetric at every lag. The same statement holds for the weak Fourier operator with positive volumetric heat capacity, symmetric positive conductivity, and reciprocal fixed boundary terms.
claims.status: internally reconstructed exact theorem; standard self-adjoint resolvent reciprocity, no novelty or nature-level claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Generic diffusion reciprocity and transient thermal rectification are established. This is a task-specific matched-port reconstruction and experimental protocol; priority is not claimed.
costs: matched, spatially calibrated heating and temperature-sensing ports
finite-volume resolution and conditioning for numerical reconstruction
claims.falsifier: With time-invariant linear reciprocal material behavior and matched calibrated ports, a reproducible H_ij(t) != H_ji(t) beyond error bars falsifies at least one premise or the operator model.
claims.next_gate: Obtain the full 2025 Su et al. article and experimental protocol; identify its exact input, output, boundary conditions, initialization energy, and rectification metric before comparing its claim to this theorem.

claims.statement: For point ports in a fixed reciprocal RC network, the temperature semigroup E(t)=exp(-C^(-1)Kt) satisfies c_i E_ij(t)=c_j E_ji(t); hence equal initial-temperature pulses have cross-response ratio E_ij/E_ji=c_j/c_i, independent of time and conductance. Equal-energy heat impulses instead have equal swapped-port temperature responses. The symmetric contrast for equal-initial-DeltaT pulses is exactly (c_j-c_i)/(c_j+c_i).
assumptions: C diagonal with strictly positive node heat capacities
same initial temperature increment in each swapped trial
claims.status: internally proved and exactly replayed on a two-node fixture; generic weighted semigroup identity is standard; experimental interface untested
claims.novelty_boundary: This is not a new heat-transfer phenomenon. It is a sharp normalization prediction distinguishing same-temperature initial conditions from equal-energy source-port transfer.
costs: independent node or patch heat-capacity measurements
claims.falsifier: For the same-DeltaT initial protocol, a time-varying cross-response ratio or a ratio inconsistent with independently measured c_j/c_i rejects the stated fixed reciprocal RC model; for equal-energy pulses, a nonzero matched-port difference rejects at least one model/calibration premise.
claims.next_gate: Run the paired initial-DeltaT/equal-energy pulse test on a graded thermal coupon with independently measured volumetric heat capacity and matched port profiles.

claims.statement: For a hydraulic graph consisting exactly of m pairwise edge-disjoint parallel corridors with corridor conductances g_i and additive corridor occlusion costs c_i, the exact minimum damage cost that reduces total conductance below G_* is min{sum_{i in I} c_i : sum_{i in I} g_i > sum_i g_i - G_*}. For rational inputs an exact 0/1 dynamic program computes this threshold in O(mW) time and O(W) memory after denominator clearing, where W=floor(L_g*(sum_i g_i-G_*))+1; this is pseudo-polynomial and the general minimum-knapsack dependence is NP-hard.
assumptions: the graph is exactly a parallel union of edge-disjoint series corridors
deleting any edge destroys its entire corridor
surviving corridor conductances remain fixed under damage
corridor occlusion costs are additive conservative lower bounds
claims.status: internally proved exact restricted-model theorem and exact rational DP; generic min-knapsack/path reasoning is standard; no physical validation or priority claim
claims.novelty_boundary: This sharpens the sufficient one-surviving-route condition in the independent fracture child report to a sharp aggregate parallel-corridor budget, but it is a standard reduced-network optimization and not a new continuum fracture result.
costs: conductance and fracture/occlusion lower bounds must be acquired per corridor
exact DP may be exponential in rational input bit length
pore geometry, uncertainty and held-out damage dominate physical cost
claims.falsifier: In the stated edge-deletion model, a subset with lost conductance above the strict threshold and cost below the computed optimum, or an exhaustive subset enumeration disagreeing with the exact DP, falsifies the calculation. Physical disagreement after graph assumptions are verified rejects the model transfer.
claims.next_gate: Use this budget on a small measured parallel-corridor microfluidic coupon, with edge conductance and occlusion-cost lower bounds independently measured.

overall_status: A precise capability boundary and falsifiable test are established for the model interface. No new material capability, validated experimental law, or priority claim is established.
